clause_evidence.reasoning: The packet contains varied applied questions requiring learners to determine elapsed times, future months, or weekdays rather than merely recite isolated facts.
Clock, calendar, and timetable samples all ask learners to reason about time in practical contexts and explicit units.
Several items use whole-hour starts and endpoints, including one-, two-, and three-hour elapsed-time problems.
Multiple clock items explicitly represent thirty-minute durations and endpoints such as 8:30, 10:30, and 11:30.
Quarter-hour problems explicitly state fifteen minutes and require learners to identify resulting :15 times.
Calendar lookup questions repeatedly require identifying weekdays for numbered dates, exercising the seven-day week labels.
Month-order and month-distance questions span many named months and require forward counting within the twelve-month year.
